newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bank sees more jobs, income growth.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bank sees more jobs, income growth.

text.p: A surge in Canada's domestic economy will spell relief on the jobs front and put more money in the pockets of Canadians during the next two years, Canada's largest bank said on Thursday.

Royal Bank of Canada said in its spring economic forecast that a rise in domestic demand will lead to the creation of 700,000 new jobs by the end of 1998 and the first increase in real disposable income since 1990.
"The long-awaited revival of Canada's domestic economy is in progress," said John McCallum, Royal Bank's chief economist.
"These additional new jobs, plus a modest rise in real wages, will allow real disposable income per capita in 1997 to increase for the first time in seven years," McCallum said.
The bank projected gross domestic product will grow by three percent in 1997 and 1998, compared to 1.5 percent last year.
The Canadian dollar is expected to end the year at C$1.3297 (US$0.7520) and increase to C$1.2804 (US$0.7810), the bank predicted.
